keyTakeawayCard.gentle: Chapter 6 explains why organizations often change only after something goes wrong. Crisis can expose the routines a system was protecting and create a brief opening for redesign. But crisis is only useful if leaders convert that exposure into better recurring habits before the system drifts back to what it already knows.
keyTakeawayCard.direct: The chapter argues that crisis weakens resistance to institutional habit change by making the cost of old routines visible. That opening matters only if it leads to durable reporting, communication, or accountability habits. Panic is not reform; replacement is.
keyTakeawayCard.competitive: Chapter 6 is about forced exposure. Crisis blows up denial and opens a window to rewrite defaults. If better habits are not installed fast, the old system comes roaring back.
